practice.heading: Build C♭ on the keyboard
practice.prompt: Select the three pitch classes that make C flat major, then check your answer.
practice.scope: This keyboard checks an unordered pitch-class set. Order, octave, fingering and live piano performance are not assessed.

content.heading: Find the notes on your keyboard
steps: Locate middle C, labeled C4. Move one semitone lower to the B3 key; read it here as C♭4.
Find E♭4 and G♭4 on black keys.
Read C♭4–E♭4–G♭4 before playing. The written octave number follows the letter C even when the accidental crosses the C/B boundary.

content.heading: Match the octave before comparing with B major
paragraphs: C♭4–E♭4–G♭4 and B3–D♯4–F♯4 have identical MIDI values: 59, 63 and 66. They describe the same physical keys with different spellings.
The prepared B-major detail page starts its root example one octave higher. Compare matched registers manually rather than assuming two page defaults should produce identical pitches.

content.heading: A reference for spelling, not a new tuning system
paragraphs: The examples use the site’s ordinary equal-tempered pitch mapping. Keeping C-flat labels does not require a special instrument or a different keyboard layout.
The first inversion is E♭4–G♭4–C♭5, labeled C♭/E♭. C♭5 uses the B4 key. Inversion and octave labels must both remain correct when these notes reach the renderer.

content.heading: Check the idea without JavaScript
paragraphs: Name the three chord tones before looking back at the answer. Then name the bass of the first inversion. These are written self-checks, not additional scored modes.
steps: First-inversion bass: E♭. The root is still C♭.

rows: No. C-flat is the white key immediately below C, normally labeled B in the same sounding register.
Octave numbers are assigned by the written letter. Lowering C4, MIDI 60, by one semitone gives C-flat4, MIDI 59, the B3 key.
Is C-flat major different from C major?
Yes. C major is C–E–G; C-flat major is C-flat–E-flat–G-flat. Every corresponding pitch is one semitone lower.
No verified hand-number examples have been prepared for this page. The missing evidence is not filled by copying another chord’s hand numbers.
Does the keyboard builder recognize enharmonic choices?
The existing builder checks sounding pitch classes rather than written spelling. C-flat and B can therefore count as the same pitch class; this is not a notation-spelling examination.

binding.tool_heading: C flat major notes and inversions
binding.answer: C-flat major contains C-flat, E-flat and G-flat. On an equal-tempered piano, its pitch classes match B, D-sharp and F-sharp.
